finishes.note: The ground body under the lawn: 0.30 of topsoil (z -0.33 to -0.03) over the whole footprint; its top carries the lawn (Planting grounds.lawn). Seen only where a cut shows it.

Parvis slabs (Story: bush-hammered, since honed would be slippery in rain), vein-cut, voids filled (walked); bands run north-south along the axis, the way one walks to the portico; weathered, soiled in the pores, worn in the lanes.

The museum's own travertine offcuts crushed (0-6 mm) and bound as a Paris-garden stabilisé: the cour, allées, cross walk, avenue, walk east, rond-point ring, path north, terrace and every building strip. Darkens when wet; trodden lanes paler.
The same stabilisé, named apart only because the canal walks (|x+44| 4.50...7.50, y 27...57) carry the exterior-walkway target.
Kerbs 0.12 wide x 0.205 deep in 1.20 lengths, sawn, top arrises chamfered 15 mm; tops worn.
The stone edge (d 1.44...1.56) of the gravel strip round the stone complex (the Rotunda's drum, the Salon, the Manet cabinet, the Nymphéas oval).
Canal and rond-point copings at sitting height 0.45: honed, weathered, with the water line (the band the water wets and stains at its level, read from the water body's level).
Canal and basin floors: Belgian bluestone, honed, permanently under water with a thin biofilm and silt, so the still water reads as a mirror (palette: Grounds canal and basin beds).

Lamp standards (post, collar, cup, finial): sand-cast CuSn10 left to weather outdoors (palette outdoors working: cast, weathered): brown-green patina, streaked below the cup, brighter where hands rub the base.
The lamps' globes: Lamberts cased opal, 3 mm (palette: Grounds lamp globes), the luminaire's diffuser; dust and rain spotting outside.
